plan: [ Single second-price auction with two opponents and no history. With independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value: it maximizes expected profit and avoids winning when the price exceeds your valuation. Overbidding risks negative payoff if the second-highest bid is above 20; underbidding risks losing profitable wins when second-highest is below 20. Therefore, bid exactly my value. ]

[ This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with 3 bidders and independent private values uniform 0–49. With risk-neutral preferences, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Underbidding risks losing profitable wins; overbidding risks winning at a loss when the second-highest value exceeds your true value. There is no past data to exploit and values redraw each round, so use truthful bidding. Thus bid exactly $28 (nearest 0.1 increment already). ]

[ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value. This maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. There is no useful history to adapt to (single round). With value $8, bidding 8 ensures: if you win, you pay the second-highest bid and profit equals 8 minus that bid; if you lose, profit is 0. Any overbid risks negative payoff; any underbid risks losing profitable wins. Bid exactly $8.0 (meets $0.1 increment rule). ]
